deals.headline: Tony Bloom acquires a majority shareholding in Union SG
deals.seller: Jürgen Baatzsch (former main shareholder and president)
deals.summary: Union SG announced that UK investor Tony Bloom, owner and chairman of Brighton & Hove Albion, had acquired a majority shareholding. Bloom would not be a director, and the club would keep a fully independent management. Alex Muzio, holding close to 10%, became chairman later in 2018. The price was not disclosed.

deals.evidence: je suis désormais l’actionnaire majoritaire de l’Union et j’augmente mon investissement dans le club
deals.headline: Alex Muzio becomes majority owner as Bloom drops to a minority for UEFA multi-club rules
deals.source_name: Royale Union Saint-Gilloise (statement by Alex Muzio, archived)
deals.summary: Union and Brighton both qualified for the 2023-24 Europa League. To comply with UEFA's multi-club ownership rules, chairman Alex Muzio became majority shareholder and increased his investment, while Tony Bloom's holding fell to a minority. Companies House records Bloom ceasing as a person with significant control of Langford Holdings on 15 June 2023.

deals.headline: Tony Bloom transfers his remaining Langford Holdings shares to Pittville Six
deals.source_name: Companies House: Langford Holdings Limited confirmation statement (CS01), 12 July 2026
deals.summary: Langford Holdings' confirmation statement of 12 July 2026 shows Anthony Grant Bloom transferring his 54,737 B ordinary shares on 25 February 2026. Pittville Six Limited, incorporated on 23 February 2026 with Michael Cotlick as its controlling person, now holds them. Alex Muzio holds 164,214 A ordinary shares. No price is filed.

name: Royale Union Saint-Gilloise
notes: Revenue is the group turnover of Langford Holdings Limited, Union's 99.44% parent (UK GAAP, in EUR, year to 30 June 2025, filed 24 March 2026). Profit on player disposals of EUR 20,608,212 is reported separately as other gains. The Belgian statutory accounts of Royale Union Saint-Gilloise SRL (KBO 0417.144.936) give chiffre d'affaires of EUR 15,029,834 and ventes et prestations of EUR 58,768,113 (including other operating income of EUR 22.9m and non-recurring income of EUR 20.8m), operating profit of EUR 2,639,151, profit before tax of EUR 2,139,776, profit of EUR 1,803,374 and staff costs of EUR 22,150,441. The 2025-26 accounts are not yet filed. The Langford group shows non-current other borrowings of EUR 44,774,583; the group owed Muzio EUR 4,515,283 under an interest-free director's loan. Langford's share split: Muzio 164,214 A ordinary shares; Pittville Six 54,737 B ordinary shares. No look-through percentage is stated, apart from Muzio's PSC band of 75% or more. Who Michael Cotlick is and whether Pittville Six has any link to Bloom is not stated. Not found on a citable page: who owns the Marien stadium (the club calls it 'our very own' and has plans for a new stadium of about 16,000 at the Bempt site in Forest, land to be bought from the municipality and the Brussels Region), attendance, shirt sponsor, kit supplier, social counts and any valuation. Honours count is as the club page states it (the 12th title was 2024-25). The club is based in Forest (Brussels-Capital Region); the city field says Brussels.

ownership_summary: Royale Union Saint-Gilloise SRL is 99.44% owned by Langford Holdings Limited (England, Companies House 11321099), whose ultimate controlling party is chairman Alex Muzio (A ordinary shares; PSC with 75% or more). Tony Bloom bought a majority in May 2018. In June 2023, to meet UEFA multi-club rules when both Union and Brighton qualified for the Europa League, Muzio became majority shareholder and Bloom dropped to a minority. On 25 February 2026 Bloom transferred his 54,737 B ordinary shares in Langford to Pittville Six Limited, a company incorporated on 23 February 2026 and controlled by Michael Cotlick.
